mirror_road_coverage — DRIVE pass op

• Data kinds: none → table (an op determined by its arguments alone — it takes no image or data input)

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.mirror_road_coverage(eye_xy, mirror_center_xy, mirror_normal_xy, mirror_width: 'float', *, mirror_radius=inf, road_point, road_direction) -> 'Dict[str, object]' (to call the implementation directly, import drivepass; drivepass.mirror_road_coverage(eye_xy, mirror_center_xy, mirror_normal_xy, mirror_width: 'float', *, mirror_radius=inf, road_point, road_direction) -> 'Dict[str, object]'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("mirror_road_coverage"))

Usage

Extent of road visible in a curve mirror (convex arc or flat) (2-D top view, closed form). Scenarios S064, S130.

The road = the straight line Q(λ) = road_point + λ·road_direction (normalised to a unit vector; placing λ = 0 at the collision point of the intersection makes it easy to read). At both ends of the mirror (for an arc, the end normals N = cos φ n ± sin φ t, φ = asin(w/2R)) the rays from the eye are reflected, and their intersections λ₁, λ₂ with the road are found. On a convex mirror the direction of the reflected ray is monotonic in the position on the mirror, so the visible range = [min λ, max λ]. If a ray does not reach the road (parallel, or pointing away), that side is ±∞ (the sign of the dot product of the ray direction and the road direction). blind_near = length from λ = 0 to the near end of the visible range (when only the part beyond 0 is visible, the blind zone just before the intersection that is not shown). Same end rays as drivedecide.convex_mirror_fov (if the eye is on the axis, the difference between the 2 directions = the full field-of-view angle).
